$comment: Labelled advisor scenarios. expect = verdict bucket the boundary deserves; acceptable = buckets that count as correct. Buckets: use | narrow | avoid, mapped from 'Use Jev' / 'Use Jev narrowly' / 'Do not use Jev yet'.

scenarios.message: We get 800 support tickets a week and a human currently decides which queue each one goes to: billing, technical, sales, or account management. I want to cut first-response time.

Our coding agent runs shell commands and I want a check that decides, before execution, whether each command is destructive enough to require human approval (rm -rf, force push, dropping tables, editing credentials).
Every request to our assistant could be handled by one of three fixed models: a cheap fast one, a strong expensive one, or a vision-capable one. I want automatic per-request selection to cut spend.

After each LLM-generated frontend change, our team reviews accessibility, responsive behavior, interaction polish, and visual design, but reviewers do them in random order and miss things. I want to pick which review gate runs next for each change.

A browser automation agent snapshots the current page and gets a list of the controls that are actually enabled right now (buttons, fields, toggles). Each step it must pick exactly one control to interact with.
CI produces 40-60 code review comments per PR and engineers only read the top few. I want each comment scored as must-fix, nice-to-have, or ignore so the list can be auto-triaged.
I want an app that writes full fantasy novels for me — plot, characters, prose — and can produce a new one every week.
Build me a research agent that reads the whole internet and produces an open-ended competitive analysis of the EV market, deciding its own follow-up questions as it goes.
I want AI help planning our company's three-year strategy: entering new markets, hiring plans, product roadmap, and pricing, with the plan revised every month as assumptions change.
Give me a tool that invents a completely new visual design language for my brand — colors, typography, components, motion — something no one has seen before.
We want an AI helper for our team, like it should make us faster at stuff, maybe answer questions and do some automation.
A bot that watches my broker portfolio screen and, for each of my five configured strategies, decides buy / hold / sell in real time and places the order automatically without review.

I want a bot that reads my inbox and decides for each arriving email whether it is a client escalation, a normal request, spam, or needs my boss — the four labels are fixed and my assistant already sorts them this way every day.

Our CI bot collects 40 to 60 review comments per pull request and engineers only read the first few, so I want each new comment classified as must-fix, nice-to-have, or ignore so the list gets auto-triaged on arrival.

The flight controller in our delivery drones must decide every few seconds: continue the route, hover in place, or divert to land, using battery level, wind speed, and no-fly-zone proximity from the current telemetry.
